blocks.text: This article provides a summary of all new features and enhancements for Secure AI Apps & Infrastructure.

blocks.heading: AI Red Teaming AI App Diagnostics

blocks.text: AIRT introduces AI App Diagnostic to validate various aspects of the application prior to running a full probe. After working with many customers, we have found that configuration and integration issues were often discovered only after a probe run had started, which caused failed or blocked runs and misleading findings. This feature will perform various validation checks to minimize any setup issues.

blocks.heading: AI Red Teaming Policy Generator support for Azure Guardrails

blocks.text: Policy Generator now supports Azure Guardrails, enabling the direct generation of policies tailored to configured AI Apps. Each generated policy includes an API Request featuring the Azure Resource Manager command required to establish the content filter policy, alongside a JSON Formatted Policy that uses Azure's RAI policy schema for the request body.

blocks.heading: AI Red Teaming Zip File Support for MCP Server Analysis

blocks.text: MCP Server Analysis now supports ZIP archive uploads. This provides customers with the ability to test private MCP servers that aren't in public repositories.
The Audit Log page in AI Guard has received the following upgrades:

blocks.item: In the Initiator column, you will now see the username and email listed instead of just the email address.
The initiator search functionality has been updated with a dropdown of usernames that can be selected.
See image.
A time range filter has been added with custom and preset ranges (Last 24 Hours, Last 7 Days, etc.).
See image.
The manual refresh button now reloads the list without reloading the entire page.
The Export CSV button downloads the filtered audit log.

blocks.text: To learn more, see AI Guard Audit Log.

blocks.item: AI Guard now supports GitHub Copilot Enterprise in Visual Studio (VS) Code.

blocks.text: AIRT now maps test results to compliance frameworks.
The Compliance Mapping page gives you one tenant-wide view of your organization's posture across frameworks.

blocks.heading: AI Red Teaming MCP Server Analysis

blocks.text: MCP Server Analysis provides visibility into the security posture of MCP servers running in the customer's environment. The analysis can be performed on both open-source MCP servers and proprietary MCP servers. A related capability, MCP Security Ratings, provides a catalog of public MCP servers and the results that have been tested by Zscaler.

blocks.heading: AI Red Teaming System Information Leakage Probe

blocks.text: AIRT introduces a new security probe: System Information Leakage.

This new probe simulates attacks that try to make the target reveal the architecture behind it: the language model and provider it runs on, whether it is a single model or a multi-agent pipeline, the tools it calls, and the infrastructure it is deployed on. The probe combines direct questions, wrong guesses, role-play, and debugging pretexts with malformed inputs that trigger raw platform errors.

In DAS mode for AI Guard: user, clientName and appName optional fields can now be included when making the DAS resolve-and-execute API call. In addition to appearing in the API, the new fields will appear on the Transaction Details window from the dashboard.
To learn more, see About AI Guard Dashboard and About AI Guard Detection Summary.

blocks.item: Webhook calls with Anthropic now display "Anthropic" as the client name in Transaction Details.

blocks.heading: AI Red Teaming AI Prefill Modal

blocks.text: AIRT is most effective when it has the proper context about an application. However, it's often not easy to obtain this context. The new AI Prefill can help with obtaining this information. Once basic connectivity has been established, AI Prefill runs a short, automated workflow against the application. Based on the responses from the application, AI Prefill suggests the Application description, Language, Multi-step attacks, and Supported modes.

blocks.heading: AI Red Teaming Connection Type Categorization Updates

blocks.text: Changes have been made to the 'Connection Type' categorization to better align with integration functionality.

blocks.item: API (No changes): REST API, PROXY SDK, OpenAI REST API.
Platform (Updated): Now includes third-party model wrappers. Added: Poe, OpenRouter, Monica, You.com, Venice, Ask AI, and CrewAI.
LLM: Reserved for direct model API integrations: Azure OpenAI, Azure ML, Anthropic, Databricks, Hugging Face, OpenAI, OpenAI Assistant, Mistral, Gemini, Bedrock, Grok, Kimi, and Perplexity.
UI/UX Consolidation: 'You.com Research' and 'You.com Answer' have been merged into a single 'You.com' card with a mode toggle, matching the pattern used for Glean.

blocks.heading: AI Red Teaming Public Agent Skills Registry

blocks.text: AIRT introduces the agent skills registry where security ratings are provided to help organizations assess the safety of public agent skills before adoption. With this feature, customers can easily assess the risks and determine whether it's suitable for deployment in production.

blocks.heading: Conversation View for Proxy Mode Transactions

blocks.text: Multi-turn conversations can now be viewed directly in the AI Guard dashboard in Proxy mode. Instead of reviewing individual transactions in isolation, admins can now see the full conversation thread, making it easier to follow the context behind a flagged or logged interaction.
See image.
From the Anthropic console, admins can now test the webhook connection with AI Guard.
See image.
To learn more, see Managing Tenant Settings.

blocks.item: Policy Control Name Column for Events: Policy Control Name is a new column added to the dashboard's events view. This gives admins clear visibility into exactly which policy control was matched for a given event, making it faster to trace and investigate policy matches.
Resizable Dashboard Columns: All columns are now resizable on the dashboard.

blocks.text: AI Guard now supports a new log export destination, CrowdStrike SIEM Direct Export, alongside the existing S3-dependent CrowdStrike option. You can now choose between exporting directly to the CrowdStrike HEC endpoint or routing event content through an intermediary AWS S3 bucket, depending on your existing setup.
See image.
To learn more, see Managing AI Guard Log Exports.

blocks.heading: New CrowdStrike Parser for AI Guard

blocks.text: CrowdStrike has updated their portal to include a new parser for AI Guard under the Generic bender connection type as zscaler-aiguard. This allows CrowdStrike users to select the AI Guard-specific parser when configuring a new data connector, rather than relying on the generic template parser.
See image.

blocks.item: Increased Topic Definition Character Limit: The character limit for Topic definitions in policy configuration has been increased from its previous limit to 1000 characters, giving admins more room to write detailed, precise topic definitions when building Topic policies.

Expanded LLM Provider Match Criteria Limit: The LLM Provider field used for match criteria in Policy control now supports up to 100 entries, up from the previous limit of 10. This allows admins to define broader and more granular policies across a wider range of LLM providers without hitting capacity constraints.

Policy Configuration Version Information: Detectors now include version information in the Policy Configuration UI in AI Guard, giving admins and security teams clearer visibility into which version of a detector is in use.
Base64 Support for Detectors: All detectors now support base64.

blocks.heading: AI Red Teaming - EU Production Environment

blocks.text: It is now possible to host the entire AI Red Teaming infrastructure within the EU. This dedicated infrastructure is specifically designed to support the unique requirements of our European customers. By utilizing this local environment, organizations can ensure enhanced performance and better alignment with regional data residency expectations. For more information, please contact your Zscaler account team.

blocks.heading: Standalone prompt hardening - Model Developer option

blocks.text: The Standalone prompt hardening feature now supports the ability to pick a model developer. This allows AIRT to generate hardening instructions that are specific to each model resulting in better protection. The supported providers are:

Anthropic
Google
Meta

blocks.heading: Event Log Export Tools Field Filter

blocks.text: Log exports can now be configured to filter out the Tools fields from exported event logs. This field is enabled by default for new and existing exports.
See image.
To learn more, see Managing AI Guard Log Exports.

AI Guard can now integrate with Anthropic Claude's inference hooks to inspect and evaluate prompts against a tenant's detection policy in real time. AI Guard responds with an Allow or Deny verdict, which determines whether Claude proceeds to generate a response or the prompt is blocked.
See image.
To learn more, see Managing Tenant Settings.

blocks.item: Malicious URL Detection in Prompt Policies: Malicious URLs can now be configured as a detection category within prompt detection policies on the policy configuration page. This expands your ability to identify and control URL-based threats embedded in user prompts.
Pattern Detector Configuration Limit Increased: The Text (Pattern) detector now supports up to 100 regex patterns per policy, increased from the previous limit of 10.
Regex Pattern Length Limit for Text Detector: Individual regex patterns in the Text (Pattern) detector can now be up to 3,000 characters in length, increased from the previous limit.

CSV Export for Dashboard Events: Dashboard event tables now support CSV export in addition to the existing PDF export option. This provides greater flexibility when sharing, analyzing, or archiving flagged interactions.

blocks.text: In AI Guard's DAS/API mode, you can now view multi-turn conversations as a single, connected thread instead of piecing together individual messages one at a time. This enhancement provides better context and visibility into flagged interactions by presenting the entire conversation flow in one unified view. All underlying data and policies remain unchanged.
See image.
To learn more, see About AI Guard Dashboard.
In the Secrets detector, the US Government ID category has been updated to support only Detect and Disable options.

Policies currently configured with BLOCK or ALLOW for this category will automatically transition to Disabled mode when any Secrets policy configuration updates are applied. All newly created policies will have the US Government ID category set to Disabled by default.
See image.
To learn more, see Adding and Managing AI Guard Policy Configurations.
Introducing support for Hybrid Workers

Customers can now deploy workers inside their own environment and avoid the need to allow any inbound connections. Workers deployed in the customer's environment make outbound connections only back to the AIRT platform and any test prompts/responses stay within the customer's network.

blocks.heading: AI Red Teaming MCP Security Ratings

blocks.text: MCP Security Ratings

MCP Security Ratings is a catalog of well-known public MCP servers that AIRT has already security-tested. Each server gets a letter grade (A to F) so you can judge its risk at a glance, then click in to see exactly which issues were found and why. Note that this feature only covers public MCP servers and not private MCP servers.

blocks.heading: AI Red Teaming Broker Support for Private Applications in AI Security Admin Portal

blocks.text: Zscaler AI Security introduces AI Red Teaming (AIRT) Broker, a more secure way to connect AIRT to customer applications without requiring firewall changes.

Previously, customers needed to whitelist AIRT source IP addresses on their firewall to allow red teaming access, a process that introduced both operational overhead and security risk. AIRT Broker eliminates this requirement by establishing inside-out connectivity, removing the need to allow any inbound access on the firewall.

Broker configuration is now manageable directly from the AI Security Admin Portal. Security teams can create and manage brokers, then assign them to specific application targets enabling AI Red Teaming to securely reach internally hosted AI applications without firewall modifications.
You can access the Brokers page from Administration > Red Teaming > Brokers.
See image.
To learn more, see Understanding the AI Security Broker, About AI Red Teaming Brokers, Connect an Asset, Registering a Broker, and Configuring a Broker Target,
AI Red Teaming introduces the Detection Level setting in probe configuration, giving security teams control over how aggressively a probe flags model responses as failures.
Three detection levels are available:

blocks.item: Strict: Flags a wider range of potentially problematic outputs, including borderline cases.
Moderate: Balances sensitivity between strict and permissive thresholds.
Permissive: Flags only high-severity violations.

blocks.text: AI Red Teaming now includes an AI Guard Tenant ID field in the Import Policy pop-up, streamlining integration with Zscaler AI Guard. Users can specify their tenant ID directly during the policy import process, eliminating the need for additional configuration steps.
See image.
AI Red Teaming adds a Rerun action at the test run level, consistent with the existing probe-level rerun behavior.

The Rerun action is available when at least one probe run is incomplete or has ended with errors. When triggered, the current vulnerability assessment resumes by rerunning all incomplete and failed probes without requiring a full test run restart. No additional units are charged for reruns, though results may vary if the test run configuration or probe versions have changed since the original run.

blocks.heading: RAG Processing Initiated from App Configuration

blocks.text: Zscaler AI Security now initiates RAG processing directly from the App Configuration page when users click Complete or Update, providing a visual progress indicator throughout the process.

Users can navigate away from the configuration screen while processing continues in the background, streamlining the overall workflow. To maintain data consistency, the system prevents new test runs from starting until RAG processing is complete and disables RAG file updates while a test run is in progress.

blocks.heading: Standalone Prompt Hardening in AI Red Teaming

blocks.text: The following changes are made as a part of this enhancement:

blocks.heading: Prompt Hardening Support for Standalone AI Applications

blocks.text: Zscaler AI Security introduces Standalone App Hardening, enabling security teams to extend prompt hardening to applications that are not yet integrated into the Zscaler AI Security asset ecosystem.

Previously, prompt hardening was only available to fully onboarded applications, leaving unmanaged and shadow apps without AI-driven security coverage. From the AI Infrastructure > Remediation page, security teams can now manually enter an application name and associate it with a business unit to generate hardened prompts without completing the standard onboarding process. This ensures that unmanaged and shadow apps receive the same AI-driven security intelligence as fully onboarded applications, giving your team consistent protection across your entire application environment.
See image.

blocks.heading: Prompt Hardening Available Without Probe Prerequisite

blocks.text: Zscaler AI Security removes the mandatory probe requirement for prompt hardening, enabling security teams to activate baseline hardening instructions from day one of onboarding.

Previously, applying prompt hardening policies required customers to onboard an application and complete a probe run first, delaying initial AI Security coverage. Probe runs and prompt hardening are now fully decoupled, allowing security teams to activate baseline hardening instructions immediately upon onboarding, apply hardening policies without completing probe configuration, and begin securing AI applications from the first day of deployment.
